# 3. Procedure for compiling an exhibit index

3.1 The index must use consecutive page numbers. A page number describes the position of a document in the bundle.

3.2 Use a short description that distinguishes each document from adjacent entries. A description such as “correspondence” is insufficient where several messages concern different requests. Do not insert a personal name merely to demonstrate how a completed entry might look.

| Index field | Requirement | Cross-reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Description | Identify the document's function | Paragraph 3.2 |
| Date | Use the document date | Paragraph 3.4 |
| Page range | Include every copied page | Schedule 2 |

3.3 Totals should state the number of documents and pages separately. A total of 24 documents and 86 pages does not establish that the bundle is complete; completeness requires comparison with the agreed list.

[^8]: Final reviewer comment: check that the cross-reference points to the correct paragraph after pagination.

[^9]: Final production comment: an empty signature field must remain empty in this specimen.
